name: Job Intelligence
description: A RAG-based system for collecting, indexing and reasoning over job descriptions.

sections.context: Job descriptions are valuable but scattered: a role disappears, a company changes its wording, and trends are hard to compare once the original page is gone.
sections.problem: Create a durable research surface that supports both exact filtering and semantic questions without turning a small research tool into an overbuilt data platform.
sections.solution: The system stores normalized job records alongside searchable document chunks. A retrieval layer grounds questions in the stored postings and returns the source material needed to inspect an answer.
sections.implementation: Ingestion is isolated from query-time work. A lightweight API coordinates extraction, validation, embedding and retrieval; the interface is deliberately thin so research remains the primary workflow.
sections.challenges: Job pages vary wildly in structure. The ingestion boundary therefore keeps raw source material and a normalized record, making extraction failures visible rather than silently losing context.
sections.outcome: A compact, inspectable prototype for comparing roles and investigating recurring requirements across a changing job market.
sections.nextIteration: Improve source attribution, add evaluation fixtures for retrieval quality, and make collection provenance more visible.

decisions.title: Relational records + vector search
decisions.decision: Keep normalized job metadata and embeddings close together.
decisions.reasoning: Research needs structured filters and semantic retrieval in the same workflow.

decisions.title: Evidence-first answers
decisions.decision: Return retrieval context with every generated response.
decisions.reasoning: It makes the system useful for research instead of presenting an opaque answer.

name: Project & Resource Planning Platform for DAF Truck
description: An internal planning platform for making project capacity, assignments and scheduling constraints visible.

sections.context: Project plans often live across spreadsheets, calendar discussions and individual assumptions. Small changes create a large amount of coordination work.
sections.problem: Give project leads a reliable view of capacity and allocation while retaining the concrete constraints behind every planning decision.
sections.solution: A shared planning model combines projects, people, assignments and time periods into one interface. Users can inspect changes before they become conflicts.
sections.implementation: The domain is modeled around scheduling concepts rather than screens. The React interface consumes a focused API and treats planning tables as a workflow, not a dashboard decoration.
sections.challenges: Scheduling logic becomes confusing when business rules are hidden in the UI. Rules were kept explicit in the domain layer and exposed in the interface where they affect a decision.
sections.outcome: A clearer operating picture for teams managing competing commitments and a foundation for incremental planning improvements.

decisions.title: Domain-led scheduling model
decisions.decision: Model assignments and availability as first-class entities.
decisions.reasoning: It keeps planning rules consistent across reports and edits.
decisions.alternative: Store a separate schedule shape for every screen.

decisions.title: Explainable conflicts
decisions.decision: Show the constraint behind an allocation warning.
decisions.reasoning: A warning is only useful when a planner can act on it.

name: Backend Engineer's Workstation
description: A static, JSON-driven portfolio designed like an internal engineering workstation.

sections.context: Most portfolios compress a body of engineering work into a familiar marketing layout. This one asks whether a portfolio can feel more like a useful technical artifact.
sections.problem: Present project thinking with a distinct visual language without obscuring the content behind dashboard theatre or decorative UI.
sections.solution: A static content repository drives reusable routes, a service registry and a command palette. The interface uses editorial whitespace and precise table-like structure instead of generic card grids.
sections.implementation: Content is validated with Zod at startup, then queried through a tiny in-memory repository. React Router resolves data-driven project pages and the production build remains static.
sections.outcome: A portfolio that can grow by adding content rather than new bespoke screens.

decisions.title: JSON as the content database
decisions.decision: Keep primary content in local JSON files.
decisions.reasoning: The site needs no runtime service and remains easy to deploy anywhere.
